main.summary: Denis Villeneuve's Dune appeared in 2021, adapting the first part of Frank Herbert's novel.

cards.heading: Dune
cards.text: Denis Villeneuve's Dune appeared in 2021, adapting the first part of Frank Herbert's novel. Paul Atreides travels with his family to Arrakis, a harsh desert planet at the centre of a struggle for power. Timothée Chalamet plays Paul alongside Rebecca Ferguson and Oscar Isaac as his parents. Villeneuve co-wrote the screenplay with Jon Spaihts and Eric Roth after joining the project in 2017. Although conceived as a two-part adaptation, only the first film was initially contracted, making continuation dependent on its reception.

main.title: Webb reveals its first science images
main.summary: NASA and its partners released the James Webb Space Telescope's first collection of full-colour science images and spectra in July 2022.

cards.heading: A new infrared view of the universe
cards.text:
NASA and its partners released the James Webb Space Telescope's first collection of full-colour science images and spectra in July 2022. A deep-field preview appeared on July 11, followed by the full collection on July 12, demonstrating the observatory's capabilities after commissioning.

Webb observes infrared light, allowing scientists to investigate distant galaxies, star formation and the atmospheres of planets beyond the Solar System. Its large mirror gathers faint light, extending the range of objects available for detailed study. The telescope is a collaboration led by NASA with the European and Canadian space agencies.

main.title: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine
main.summary: On 24 February 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, starting the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II, in a major escalation of the existing war between the two countries that began when Russia attacked Ukraine in 2014.

cards.heading: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine
cards.text:
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, escalating the war that had begun in 2014. The fighting caused hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of Ukrainian civilian casualties. Russian forces occupied roughly a fifth of Ukraine, while about eight million Ukrainians were internally displaced and six to seven million fled abroad.

Russia had massed troops near Ukraine's borders in late 2021 and demanded, among other conditions, that Ukraine be barred from joining NATO. Vladimir Putin announced the invasion as a special military operation in support of the Russian-backed separatist republics of Donetsk and Luhansk. His stated justification challenged Ukraine's legitimacy as an independent state.

main.title: The Batman
main.subtitle: A detective follows Gotham through its secrets
main.summary: Matt Reeves' The Batman introduces Robert Pattinson as a young Gotham vigilante. A series of killings brings him into contact with Selina Kyle and the Riddler. Released in the United States on 4 March 2022, the film follows clues through a city whose officials and criminal networks are closely entangled.

cards.heading: A case for the detective
cards.text: Matt Reeves' The Batman introduces Robert Pattinson as a young Gotham vigilante. A series of killings brings him into contact with Selina Kyle and the Riddler. Released in the United States on 4 March 2022, the film follows clues through a city whose officials and criminal networks are closely entangled.

cards.heading: Following the connections
cards.text: Batman works beside James Gordon at crime scenes, studying messages left for him and following the connections between victims. Selina brings another view of the people caught inside Gotham's power structures. The investigation reaches Bruce Wayne's own family, making the city's corruption a personal problem. Reeves lets questions and discoveries carry much of the film. The masked figure is useful as an investigator, but fear alone gives him a limited answer to the suffering around him.

cards.heading: What Gotham needs
cards.text: Greig Fraser's photography makes rain, darkness and harsh pools of light part of Gotham's atmosphere. The restrained visibility suits an investigation in which each room or street may conceal another piece of information. Michael Giacchino's recurring musical motif gives Batman a deliberate presence. Against that weight, the film develops a question about what he can offer the city: his role begins to extend from punishing its criminals toward helping the people left in their path.

main.title: Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore
main.subtitle: Dumbledore entrusts a divided mission to an unlikely team
main.summary: Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore brings Newt Scamander into a mission organized by Albus Dumbledore to resist Grindelwald's growing influence. David Yates directs, with J.K. Rowling and Steve Kloves sharing screenplay credit. The film opened in Britain and Ireland on 8 April 2022, followed by the United States on 15 April.

cards.heading: A team against Grindelwald
cards.text: Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore brings Newt Scamander into a mission organized by Albus Dumbledore to resist Grindelwald's growing influence. David Yates directs, with J.K. Rowling and Steve Kloves sharing screenplay credit. The film opened in Britain and Ireland on 8 April 2022, followed by the United States on 15 April.

cards.heading: Plans within plans
cards.text: Jude Law's Dumbledore cannot confront Grindelwald directly, so he relies on Newt and a group whose members have different skills and incomplete information. Jacob Kowalski, still a non-magical baker, joins witches and wizards including Eulalie Hicks and Theseus Scamander. Mads Mikkelsen takes over as Grindelwald. The separate assignments make uncertainty part of the team's strategy, as the characters try to prevent their opponent from anticipating a single, easily understood plan.

cards.heading: Creatures and political power
cards.text: The mission connects Newt's knowledge of magical animals to a contest for leadership. His instinct to protect vulnerable creatures becomes important within institutions that are willing to use them for another purpose. The film also returns to the relationship between Dumbledore and Grindelwald, placing their private history beside the public consequences of their conflict. James Newton Howard continues as composer; The Room We Require recalls the series' connection to Hogwarts while accompanying the preparations for this wider journey.

main.title: Genocide in Gaza
main.subtitle: Civilian devastation and international accountability
main.summary: The Gaza genocide is the ongoing, intentional, and systematic destruction of the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip carried out by Israel during the Gaza war.

cards.heading: The destruction of Palestinian life
cards.text: The Gaza genocide is the ongoing, intentional, and systematic destruction of the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip carried out by Israel during the Gaza war. It encompasses mass killings, the targeted killing of children (who account for 30% of those killed), deliberate starvation, infliction of serious bodily and mental harm, and prevention of births. Other acts include blockading, destroying civilian infrastructure, destroying healthcare facilities, killing healthcare workers and aid-seekers, causing mass forced displacement, committing sexual violence, and destroying educational, religious, and cultural sites.

cards.heading: International recognition
cards.text: The genocide has been recognized, in either a legal or scholarly sense, by a United Nations special committee and commission of inquiry, the International Association of Genocide Scholars, multiple human rights groups, state governments, numerous genocide studies and international law scholars, and other experts.

main.title: Paris 2024 Olympic Games
main.summary: Paris hosted the Olympic Games from 26 July to 11 August 2024, with some competitions beginning on 24 July.

cards.heading: Paris 2024 Olympic Games
cards.text: Paris hosted the Olympic Games from 26 July to 11 August 2024, with some competitions beginning on 24 July. Events extended across France: Marseille staged sailing, other cities hosted football, and Tahiti held the surfing competition. Paris became the second city to host the Summer Games three times, following its editions in 1900 and 1924. The IOC had awarded Paris the event in 2017 while also assigning the 2028 Games to Los Angeles. The organisation linked the capital's central role to sporting venues spread well beyond it.

main.title: Nobel Prize in Literature: László Krasznahorkai
main.summary: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the Hungarian novelist László Krasznahorkai (born 1954) "for his compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art." He is the second Hungarian Nobel laureate in Literature after Imre Kertész in 2002.

main.title: Nobel Prize in Literature: Anne Carson
main.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian poet Anne Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature."
